scenarios.candidate_claim: A clean merge has already created a merge commit, so every integration correction requires amend or history rewrite.

materials.trigger_query: Git merged this cleanly. Reconcile both branches and keep the integration correction in the merge result.
skill_rules: Only when MERGE_HEAD exists, continue an already active merge.
Otherwise inspect ancestry and preview the merge first.
For a new execution request, run git merge --no-commit --no-ff only after the preview.

scenarios.candidate_claim: The confirmed state and production rule leave no permitted completion path without amend or history rewrite.

materials.runtime_trace: git show -s --format=%P HEAD reports two parents; MERGE_HEAD is absent because the merge commit already exists.
materials.user_requirement: Do not amend or rewrite existing history.
materials.skill_rule: All later integration corrections for this task must be inserted into that existing merge commit.
materials.task_requirement: The integration correction is required before the task can complete.
materials.alternative_path_check: The target materials define no other permitted completion path.
materials.reproduced_failure: Following the Skill rule requires a forbidden history rewrite; following the user requirement violates the Skill completion rule.

scenarios.candidate_claim: Two potentially overlapping descriptions make both Skills load and issue conflicting actions in the same run.

materials.skill_a_description: Review or clarify a proposed implementation plan.
materials.skill_b_description: Review an existing implementation requirement before coding.

scenarios.candidate_claim: The two production Skills impose irreconcilable actions on one reachable request and cause a repeatable failure.

materials.client_rule: The target client loads every matching project Skill for this request type.
materials.load_trace: The same request loaded skill-a and skill-b in three of three runs.
materials.skill_a_rule: Before the first file edit, call reserve-write.
materials.skill_b_rule: For this request, do not call any tool before the first file edit.
materials.applicability: Both rules apply before the same first file edit and neither declares an exception.
materials.failure_trace: All three runs stopped before editing because no action could satisfy both rules.
